messages:

Subject: On-prem deployment questions: jurisdiction & audit access

Connor / David —

Thanks for the demo last week. We're moving toward an order form for an on-prem (VPC) install for two environments: Production (us-east-1) and Analytics (eu-west-1). Before procurement can sign, our legal team has two hard asks:

1) License scope: we need explicit confirmation that runtime binaries shipped under the Order Form are limited to the customer-executed runtime (no source-code handover or derivative rights).

2) Audit access model: MediProbe requires an evidence path for regulatory audits — ideally a quarterly forensic snapshot or a live audit window where our auditors can observe ingestion and retention controls. We are open to options but need a documented flow and timeline.

Attached is our procurement checklist (see referenced items). Please confirm what Redwood can provide and any constraints.

Also include a point of contact for legal to coordinate redlines to the MSA addendum.

Thanks —
Samantha Park
Head of Procurement, MediProbe

Subject: Re: On-prem deployment questions: jurisdiction & audit access

Samantha —

Appreciate the clear checklist. Quick responses up front:

- License boundary: Redwood will not transfer source code or grant derivative rights. The Order Form + MSA Annex will specify a limited "runtime license" for the delivered artifacts and operator tooling.

- Audit access: We typically offer two paths: (A) time-limited, read-only audit sessions to the hosted management console (tokenized, logged, and scoped), or (B) forensic snapshot delivery under NDA with PII redaction options.

For on-prem/VPC deployments we prefer model (A) as a production-safe first choice; model (B) can be arranged for high-compliance customers but needs a controlled delivery and proof-of-destruct procedure. I've attached a draft addendum (Proposed_Addendum_v1.docx) that maps both options into Annex C and suggests an audit window workflow.

Next step: looping in Laura from Legal and Marissa (Solutions) to propose concrete redlines and an Order Form exhibit. Laura — would you be able to take a pass and propose language that avoids perpetual deposit of artifacts while meeting MediProbe's audit needs?

Connor O'Brien
Senior Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Samantha / Connor —

I've reviewed Proposed_Addendum_v1 and sketched redlines. High-level stance from legal: we cannot accommodate full, unrestricted deposit of runtime images into customer custody or third-party escrow without a narrowly-scoped trigger and technical controls. Key points in the redline (attached as Proposed_Addendum_v2_redlines.docx):

- Replace "forensic snapshot deposit" with a "sealed snapshot retrieval process". In practice this means Redwood will:
  * Provide a time-limited, read-only remote audit session for certified auditors (two options: live observation or recorded session with tamper-evident logs).
  * For exceptional situations (regulatory subpoena / court order), supply a sealed runtime image to a mutually agreed third-party custodian on a one-off basis under strict access conditions.

- Add explicit PII-sanitization and hash-verification steps for any image release.

- Limit jurisdictional transfer clauses: images and artifacts will be transferred only if the customer provides evidence of legal entitlement and the transfer complies with export controls.

- We propose a 30-day mutually-agreed audit window cadence (quarterly by default) with 7 days' notice. We resisted any language that requires perpetual escrow.

I've inserted text to the MSA Annex for: scope of license (runtime-only), operator credentials (rotated, scoped, auditable), and the audit remediation timeline. I've also included a DocuSign envelope link to the draft addendum for your reference.

If MediProbe agrees on the sealed-snapshot-with-custodian compromise, we can finalize redlines and fold the exhibit into the Order Form.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Proposed_Addendum_v2_redlines.docx (redline), sample-custodian-agreement.pdf (stub)

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple of procurement items we need to close before final signature:

1) Witness inspection window: MediProbe would like a one-week witness inspection (on-prem or remote) per year. Can Redwood commit to scheduling windows and providing an SLA credit if missed?

2) Order Form exhibit: please add the specific exhibit reference and the deployment regions (us-east-1, eu-west-1). We need that for our risk committee.

3) Pricing carveout: because the sealed-snapshot path is a higher-touch operation, how will Redwood price that work and will it be a one-time fee or ongoing? Please loop in your finance/pricing contact if necessary.

We can move quickly if we get a redline response and the price delta for the custodial snapshot option. HubSpot deal is MP-2023-1184; PV expects a PO within 10 business days once language and pricing are agreed.

Thanks everyone — quick summary and next steps so there's no ambiguity:

Agreed posture:
- License scope: runtime-only license; no source code or derivative rights. (See Annex language in Proposed_Addendum_v2_redlines).
- Audit model: default = quarterly, time-limited read-only audit sessions (7 days' notice). Exceptional sealed-snapshot to a third-party custodian only on a narrowly-scoped trigger; Redwood will provide PII-sanitization options and hash verification before transfer.
- Regions: the Order Form exhibit will enumerate us-east-1 and eu-west-1.
- Witness inspection: Redwood will offer a one-week witness inspection window per year; SLA credit terms to be provided by Pricing.
